title: The Winter Regiment
premise: In 1913, Ada Winterbourne drives for a prominent suffragist and quietly reads the movement's letters, memorizing names and secrets she was never meant to know. When a scarred stranger arrives with a letter in the handwriting of Captain Elias Thorn — a man officially dead since the Boer War and now branded a traitor — Ada recognizes the script as one she has copied herself, and realizes her employer's network is entangled in his survival. Hunted by military intelligence and betrayed from within their own circle, Ada and Elias follow a trail of coded correspondence to the river town where his innocence can be proven. At the breaking of the ice, Ada must honor a peacetime promise she made to Elias's sister: that if he ever came back, someone would stand witness for him. She does — at cost to her name, her position, and nearly her life — and the regiment of strangers who sheltered them becomes the family she never had.
about_author: Wren Okafor is a former archivist who spent years cataloguing suffragist correspondence in regional collections, where the margins told louder stories than the letters themselves. The Winter Regiment is a debut novel born from a single misfiled envelope and the question of who keeps secrets for people they love.

chapters.title: The Letters Before the Names
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We meet her steaming open envelopes in a Bloomsbury kitchen, fluent in other people's handwriting and careful to be invisible. A letter arrives bearing the unmistakable hand of Elias Thorn — dead seven years, officially. Emotional beat: the thrill and guilt of secret knowledge turning to dread.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Mews
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The stranger, gaunt and army-broken, delivers a second Thorn letter addressed not to the movement but to 'the driver who reads.' He knows what she does. He asks her to carry word to a safehouse before military intelligence closes the net. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Mistress Knew
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with an interlude of Lady Verity's diary pages. Ada confronts her employer obliquely and discovers Verity has been funding Thorn's hiding since the war — and that someone inside the circle recently sold information. Beat: loyalty shaken; the found-family begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Ice Road South
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Flashback chapters braided forward: how he survived, why he was declared dead, and the promise Ada made to his sister Margaret in 1908 — witnessed at a garden meeting, sealed with a borrowed pen. Beat: grief and tenderness; stakes become personal.

chapters.title: Handwriting and Lies
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Military intelligence officer Colonel Ashe summons her, courteous and venomous, offering immunity to betray Verity. Ada lies fluently for the first time in her careful life — and realizes the traitor's letters match Ashe's own clerk. Beat: quiet fury; Ada becomes an actor, not a bystander.

chapters.title: The River Town Registry
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ada and Elias travel under false papers to Marlowe Bend, where the parish registry holds proof Thorn reported a war crime his superiors buried. They find the registry page razored out — but the vicar's daughter kept a copied ledger. Beat: hope rekindled, then hunted.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Bell Loft
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The stranger from Chapter 2 sells them out; soldiers surround the church while Ada hides the copied ledger against her skin. Elias surrenders himself to buy her escape, echoing his sister's sacrifice years before. Beat: heartbreak; the promise now falls wholly on Ada.

chapters.title: The Regiment Assembles
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The scattered network — laundresses, a railway porter, Verity herself arriving uninvited — becomes an improvised regiment to move Elias from custody to the assize court before the river ice breaks and evidence routes reopen. Beat: solidarity; found family forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Before the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax. In the courtroom, Ada stands as witness, reading aloud the letter she first opened in Chapter 1 and producing the copied ledger, implicating Ashe. Ashe's men attempt seizure; the townsfolk physically bar the doors. Beat: terror transfigured into courage; the promise kept aloud.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue-like. Elias is cleared; Ashe is ruined; Verity offers Ada her freedom and, unexpectedly, a partnership. On the riverbank as the ice breaks, Ada chooses neither servant nor fugitive life but her own name, spoken plainly among the people who stood for her. Beat: release, identity claimed, family chosen.
